article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 100% Indica
Genetics: Red River Delta × Master Kush
Breeder: Barney’s Farm
THC Content: 21–24%
CBD Content: 1-1.4% l
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Papaya, mango, lavender, hazelnut, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 55–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: end of September
Indoor Yield: 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 800 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Ayahuasca Purple looks almost engineered for the moment when a grower opens the flowering room and simply stops to stare. Broad leaves surround thick purple and ruby-colored buds, orange pistils disappear beneath resin, and the compact plant carries flowers disproportionately large for its relatively short frame. Yet appearance is only half of its identity. Barney’s Farm created this pure indica by combining Red River Delta with Master Kush, producing marijuana that moves away from the familiar grape-and-berry profile associated with many purple strains .

Instead, the aroma leans toward papaya, mango, lavender, roasted nuts, earth, and exotic spice. The experience follows an equally distinctive path, beginning with contentment and euphoria before settling into deep physical relaxation. For consumers interested in colorful old-school indica weed and growers looking for a short, productive plant with a fast finish, this cultivar offers considerably more than dramatic pigmentation.
Genetics and Lineage

Ayahuasca Purple originated after Barney’s Farm received Red River Delta seeds and discovered unusually colorful plants within the material. Those specimens produced striking purple and ruby hues along with a sturdy, broad-leaf structure that made them attractive breeding candidates. Rather than preserving the line unchanged, the breeders paired selected Red River Delta genetics with Master Kush, reinforcing compact indica architecture, resin production, flower density, and physical potency. The resulting cross was stabilized around an essentially pure indica expression.

Red River Delta remains the more mysterious half of the pedigree because its deeper ancestry has not been extensively documented by the breeder. Master Kush is far better established. Barney’s Farm describes its Master Kush material as descending from Hindu Kush landrace genetics originating in the Afghan Hindu Kush region, a historic center of resinous broad-leaf cannabis and traditional hash production. These genetics contribute tightly spaced branches, large fan leaves, earthy incense-like aromas, and exceptionally dense flowers.

Combining the two parents produced a cultivar with unusual visual consistency. Purple coloration is genetically embedded rather than dependent entirely on cold temperatures, although cooler nights late in bloom can intensify anthocyanin expression. The Kush ancestry also explains why the plant stays comparatively short while supporting substantial flower weight. Instead of stretching aggressively, it concentrates energy into thick colas on a compact framework.
Effects and Experience

The first stage is often more euphoric than the plant’s heavy indica appearance suggests. A warm improvement in mood may develop quickly, accompanied by contentment, easy conversation, and a temporary sense that ordinary concerns have become less important. Rather than creating the sharp cerebral acceleration associated with Haze-heavy cannabis, the mental shift tends to feel immersive and dreamlike. Some consumers describe an unusually introspective quality at stronger doses, which likely contributed to the strain’s evocative name.

Physical relaxation gradually becomes the dominant feature. Limbs can feel heavier, muscular tension recedes, and remaining in one comfortable position begins to seem increasingly appealing. The transition is usually smooth rather than abrupt, allowing the initial euphoric phase to blend into deeper calm. With THC reaching roughly 24%, larger servings may produce substantial couch-lock and sleepiness, making evening use a more natural fit than mornings requiring concentration or coordination.

Experienced marijuana consumers may find the strain deeply relaxing without feeling immediately incapacitated, while people with limited tolerance should start cautiously. High doses of THC can still produce dizziness, dry mouth, dry eyes, temporary anxiety, or disorientation. Because potency varies between plants and harvests, the cannabinoid analysis on the actual flower remains more informative than the strain name alone.
Medical Benefits

The heavy physical character may appeal to medical cannabis patients seeking relief from persistent discomfort, muscular tension, or difficulty settling down in the evening. THC can influence pain perception through the endocannabinoid system and other neurological pathways, while the cultivar’s relaxing effect may make background aches feel less intrusive. Its relatively small amount of CBD does not make it a balanced THC/CBD strain, but it may provide slightly more cannabidiol than many modern high-THC varieties.

Sleep is another reason patients may investigate this type of cannabis. The later stages can become noticeably sedating, particularly after larger doses, and the gradual transition from mental ease into physical heaviness may suit people whose nighttime problems involve both stress and bodily tension. Appetite stimulation may also occur, as is common with THC-rich marijuana, although the intensity differs substantially between individuals.

Myrcene, caryophyllene, and pinene add additional chemical complexity. Myrcene contributes earthy and herbal qualities, while beta-caryophyllene creates peppery warmth and is unusual among common cannabis terpenes because it can interact with CB2 receptors. These compounds remain subjects of ongoing research, but terpene presence alone should not be interpreted as proof of a specific therapeutic outcome. Patients using cannabis for a diagnosed condition should consider dose, medication interactions, and their own response to THC.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Ayahuasca Purple avoids the predictable grape flavor associated with many violet-colored marijuana varieties . Tropical fruit appears instead. Papaya and mango form a soft, ripe sweetness, while floral lavender adds an almost perfumed quality. Beneath those brighter notes sits an earthy Kush foundation accompanied by a distinctive nutty character frequently compared with hazelnut. Breaking apart the flower can reveal additional pungency and light spice.

The terpene profile helps explain that unusual combination. Myrcene brings earth, musk, herbs, and ripe-fruit depth, while beta-caryophyllene introduces spice and dryness. Pinene adds a cleaner resinous edge that prevents the profile from becoming excessively sweet. Depending on phenotype and cultivation conditions, one harvest may lean heavily tropical while another emphasizes nuts, flowers, and dark earth.

On inhalation, sweet fruit generally arrives before the heavier flavors. Mango and papaya can give way to lavender, nuts, herbs, and earthy spice through the exhale. Vaporization tends to preserve more of the floral and tropical top notes, whereas combustion emphasizes Kush earthiness and pungency. Slow drying and controlled curing are particularly important for maintaining the more delicate fruit aromatics.
Growing Information

This cultivar grows like a classic broad-leaf indica. Indoor plants generally remain around 90–110 centimeters tall, forming thick stems, large fan leaves, close internodal spacing, and a short heavyset silhouette. Outdoors, plants commonly reach approximately 120–150 centimeters. Because vertical stretch is limited, the genetics fit grow tents and rooms where height is restricted. Topping or gentle low-stress training can broaden the canopy, although excessive manipulation is rarely necessary to keep the plant manageable.

Flowering takes approximately 55–65 days. During the final weeks, flowers become exceptionally dense and the purple coloration intensifies, sometimes spreading across leaves as well as buds. One practical issue becomes increasingly important near harvest: branch support. Colas can become heavy enough to bend or break limbs, so stakes, plant ties, or trellis netting should be installed before weight becomes a problem. Indoor production typically falls around 500–600 grams per square meter when lighting, irrigation, root health, and environmental control are optimized.

Outdoor plants can produce roughly 800 grams each under strong sunlight and favorable conditions, with harvest usually arriving during the third or fourth week of September. That relatively early finish is useful in climates where autumn rain develops quickly. Dense buds still demand careful humidity management, however. Good spacing, interior airflow, and protection from prolonged wet weather reduce the risk of moisture becoming trapped within mature colas. The plant’s combination of manageable size, relatively fast flowering, sturdy growth, and strong yield potential makes it approachable for newer growers while still rewarding experienced cultivators who fine-tune the environment.
FAQ
Is Ayahuasca Purple an indica or sativa?

Ayahuasca Purple is a 100% indica according to Barney’s Farm. Its broad leaves, compact growth, dense flowers, limited stretch, and deeply relaxing later effects all reflect its indica heritage. Despite that classification, the initial experience can still contain noticeable euphoria and sociability before physical relaxation takes over.
What strains make Ayahuasca Purple?

The genetics are Red River Delta crossed with Master Kush. Barney’s Farm received Red River Delta seeds and selected especially attractive purple and ruby-colored plants before combining them with Master Kush. The Master Kush side contributes Hindu Kush-derived structure, resin, earthiness, and traditional indica characteristics.
How strong is Ayahuasca Purple?

Breeder information places THC around 21–24%, making it a potent cannabis strain without reaching the extreme 30% figures associated with some contemporary hybrids. Its heavy indica effects can nevertheless feel powerful, particularly during the later stages. Dose and tolerance play a major role in determining intensity.
What does Ayahuasca Purple taste like?

The flavor combines papaya, mango, lavender, hazelnut, earth, herbs, and mild spice. Unlike many purple weed strains that emphasize grape or berry, this cultivar has a distinctly tropical and nutty character. Myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and pinene contribute to its earthy, spicy, and resinous background.
How long does Ayahuasca Purple take to flower?

Indoor flowering normally takes approximately 55–65 days. Outdoors, plants are generally ready during the third or fourth week of September in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Growers should still check trichome maturity and flower development rather than relying entirely on a calendar date.
Final Thoughts on Ayahuasca Purple

Ayahuasca Purple stands apart because its appearance, aroma, and growth pattern all reinforce a clear identity. Red River Delta contributes dramatic violet and ruby pigmentation, while Master Kush adds the compact structure, dense resinous flowers, earthy depth, and deeply relaxing character associated with Hindu Kush cannabis. The result is a true indica that does not need an exaggerated flowering time or enormous plant size to produce impressive harvests.

Its sensory profile is equally distinctive. Papaya and mango replace the predictable grape flavor of many purple cultivars, while lavender, hazelnut, earth, and spice create an unusually complex finish. A euphoric opening gradually gives way to heavy physical relaxation, making the strain best suited to slower evenings when demanding tasks are finished.

For growers, a short 55–65 day flowering period, compact 90–110 centimeter indoor stature, strong purple expression, and yields approaching 600 g/m² create a practical combination of visual appeal and productivity. For consumers, the attraction lies in something less measurable: an old-school indica experience wrapped in unusually exotic aromatics. Ayahuasca Purple is not simply purple marijuana with a memorable name; it is a carefully selected Kush-based cultivar whose genetics, color, tropical-nutty flavor, and powerful physical finish give it a personality of its own.
